standard_prerequisites.name: For a flat local ring map whose special fibre has dimension zero, the dimension of the source equals the dimension of the target, and more generally the dimension formula expressing dim(B) through dim(A) and the fibre

standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the chain of equalities that makes dim(B over q) independent of q and gives the two dimension identities used for A.

standard_prerequisites.name: A Noetherian local ring is catenary exactly when the assignment sending a prime to the dimension of the quotient is a dimension function, i.e. drops by exactly one along each immediate specialization
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the formula obtained for immediate specializations into the catenarity of A.

core_obligations: Let p be a prime of A and q a prime of B minimal over pB; record that q lies over p by going down, so that A_p -> B_q is a flat local ring map with zero dimensional special fibre (proof lines 32400-32405).

Use the dimension formula for such a map together with the equidimensionality and catenarity of B to write dim(A_p) = dim(B_q) = dim(B) - dim(B/q), and conclude that dim(B/q) does not depend on the choice of q, so that B over pB is equidimensional of dimension dim(B) - dim(A_p) (proof lines 32406-32413).

Use the flat dimension identities dim(B over pB) = dim(A over p) + dim(B over m_A B) and dim(B) = dim(A) + dim(B over m_A B) to deduce dim(A_p) = dim(A) - dim(A over p) for every prime p, and conclude that A is equidimensional by applying this to the minimal primes (proof lines 32413-32423).

Prove catenarity: for a strict inclusion p contained in p' with no prime in between, apply the same computation to the prime p' over p in A over p, using that A over p -> B over pB is flat with equidimensional target, to get 1 = dim((A over p)_{p'}) = dim(A over p) - dim(A over p'), so that the assignment p maps to dim(A over p) is a dimension function and A is catenary (proof lines 32424-32434).
proof_roadmap: Choose a prime q of B minimal over pB and use flatness and zero dimensional special fibre to compute dim(A_p) through dim(B) and dim(B/q) (proof lines 32400-32410).
Read off that B over pB is equidimensional of a dimension independent of q, which is conclusion (1) (proof lines 32411-32413).
Apply the flat dimension identities to obtain dim(A_p) = dim(A) - dim(A over p) and conclude that A is equidimensional (proof lines 32413-32423).
Repeat the computation for immediate specializations to see that the dimension of the quotient drops by one, which is exactly catenarity of A (proof lines 32424-32434).
difficulty_reason: The statement says that for a flat local homomorphism A -> B of local Noetherian rings with B catenary and equidimensional, the fibres B over pB stay equidimensional and the source A is again catenary and equidimensional (statement lines 32388-32397). The proof reduces everything to one dimension computation: for a prime q minimal over pB the special fibre of A_p -> B_q is zero dimensional, so dim(A_p) equals dim(B_q), and equidimensionality plus catenarity of B make dim(B/q) independent of q (proof lines 32400-32413). The same computation applied to the quotients by a prime gives the dimension formula for A, and applied to an immediate specialization it shows that the dimension function drops by exactly one, which is the catenarity criterion (proof lines 32413-32434). The references to the dimension formula and to going down are pointers to standard results of another chapter; the argument that turns them into the two conclusions is inside the counted span.
